newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says EU states assured it ties to continue.
newsitem.headline: Iran says EU states assured it ties to continue.

text.p: Iran's foreign minister said on Monday some European Union states had assured Tehran their decision to withdraw their ambassadors was not intended to damage ties with Iran.

EU member states, except Greece, have said they would recall their Tehran ambassadors for consultations after a German court ruled on Thursday that top Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killing of four Kurdish Iranian dissidents in Berlin.

"Certain ambassadors of important European states have clearly stated in contacts with us during the past few days that they did not want their temporary departure from Tehran to be taken as an unfriendly act by their countries' governments," said Ali Akbar Velayati in remarks reported by Tehran radio.

"He (Velayati) said the diplomatic envoys of these countries intend to return to Tehran and are determined to preserve and develop their high-level ties with the Islamic Republic of Iran," the state-run radio said. He did not name any of the countries.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the killings which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.
Iran has responded to the withdrawals of the envoys by announcing it will recall its envoys in return.
Velayati said the future of ties with Germany depended mostly on Bonn's actions, it added. "Iran was not the party that began wrecking Tehran-Bonn relations."
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Monday Bonn had no reason to doubt assurances from Tehran that Germans were safe in Iran despite mass protests there against the verdict.
Germany or any other country that "crosses the line" over Iranian foreign policy principles would be confronted with Iran's "decisive policy and stance", Velayati added.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Friday blamed the move on a plot by Israel and the United States -- Iran's arch-enemies -- and said the row was a "passing storm".
Germany made clear at the weekend it would seek to avoid stepping up the dispute with Iran over the ruling.

Bonn officials say privately that, behind the scenes, Iran has signalled it does not wish to raise the temperature in the diplomatic stand-off with a country which, until recently, was its biggest trade partner and friend in the West.
